question.text: The Democratic Unionist Party has long been the majority party in Northern Ireland's parliament, which convenes at Stormont Castle in this capital city.
question.clue: A major politician in this city was the founder of the Martyrs Memorial Free Presbyterian Church, Ian Paisley, whose Democratic Unionist party brought him to power.

swap.leadin: Taoiseach [pr. TEA-SHICH] Brian Cowen, the prime minister of this nation, was incriminated in 2009 after revelations that this country's central bank had hidden millions of euros worth of loans.
swap.text: Name this country which was partitioned in two in 1920, then declared a "Free State" two years later.
swap.clue: A civil war erupted in this country between pro and anti-treaty forces led by Michael Collins and Eamon de Valera, respectively.

question.text: Domestically, Blair negotiated this agreement, which released IRA prisoners and ended the Troubles.
question.clue: Bertie Ahern and David Andrews were signatories of this document, which was primarily negotiated by David Trimble and John Hume.

swap.leadin: It was led by Patrick Pearse and Tom Clarke.
swap.text: Name this 1916 revolt in which rebels took over the General Post Office and other buildings until they were defeated and executed by the British. William Butler Yeats wrote a poem about this event.
swap.answerHtml: Easter Rising [accept Easter Rebellion, or anything else involving people revolting and Easter]
swap.clue: This event was reduced in scope after a ship carrying smuggled German weapons was captured, despite the efforts of Roger Casement.

question.text: The Dail Eireann sits in this city, the capital of Ireland.
question.clue: This city's King Imar was likely the same person as Ragnar Lodbrok's son Ivar the Boneless.

swap.text: The revolution wasn't completely bloodless, as over 2,000 people were killed at this 1690 battle at which William decisively defeated James II.
swap.clue: Commemorated by a contemporary holiday called The Twelfth, this battle was followed a year later by the loser's successful defense of Limerick.

question.leadin: This movement provides its name to four bills, the third of which was passed in 1914 but never implemented due to World War I.
question.text: Name this movement calling for the self-governance of a former country of the United Kingdom.
question.answerHtml: Irish Home Rule [prompt on just “Home Rule”; prompt on “Irish Independence,” “Irish autonomy,” or other similar answers]
question.clue: Anti-Papist fears were cited by opponents of this cause, such as the Orange League.

swap.leadin: This event was carried out by James Carey and other members of the Invincibles.
swap.text: Name this event in which Frederick Cavindish and Thomas Henry Burke were fatally stabbed.
swap.clue: It resulted in the death of a man married to Prime Minister Gladstone's niece.

question.leadin: Name these members of the Irish Republican Army.
question.text: He was the first of ten Maze Prison hunger strikers to die in 1981 during a protest to expand the privileges given to IRA-affiliated inmates.
question.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

swap.leadin: "I ran away with two old people, but they were caught and killed, and the soldiers made me carry the baskets holding their cut-off hands."
swap.text: These horrors were described in a 1903 report by this Irish diplomat and activist. This man detailed systematic abuses being perpetrated in the Congo Free State.
swap.clue: This man's lawyer, A. M. Sullivan, tried to argue that there was a comma after the word "realm" in the clause "realm or elsewhere" in the 1351 statute this man was charged with violating; as a result, this man was said to have been "hanged on a comma."

question.text: This man also took part in the Easter Rebellion. As the IRA Director of Intelligence, he was a leader of the Irish War of Independence, and he signed the unpopular Anglo-Irish Treaty.
question.clue: This leader of an assassination group known as The Squad was imprisoned at Frongoch internment camp for their role as aide-de-camp to Joseph Plunkett during the Easter Rising.

swap.text: After the 1918 election, members of this political party created the Irish Parliament that supported the IRA. This still-existing political party has a name meaning "we ourselves."
swap.clue: Former Tanaiste Eamon Gilmore was originally a member of this party before eventually joining the Labour Party.

question.leadin: Identify the following about David Ricardo's worst nightmare--the Corn Laws.
question.text: The Corn Laws began to be repealed with the onset of this event, which lasted from 1845 to around 1850 and had its effects worsened by the Gregory clause. Many then emigrated from the Emerald Isle to countries like the U.S.
question.clue: Protestant missionaries set up schools during this event in an act called "souperism."

swap.text: The Armagh disturbances were part of a conflict in this historic province, much of which now makes up Northern Ireland. The Scots-Irish principally lived in this northernmost province.
swap.clue: This province was the site of an early 17th century "plantation," in which James I settled thousands of Scots here.

question.text: Before founding the British Union of Fascists, Oswald Mosley left the Conservative Party for the Labour Party over the use of this anti-IRA unit of the British Army. They took their name from the colors of their mixed uniforms.
question.answerHtml: Black and Tans [or Royal Irish Constabulary Special Reserve]
question.clue: Members of this group were paid just 10 shillings per day, and most were veterans of World War I. This group killed 12 people in Croke Park at a football match in the aftermath of Bloody Sunday.

swap.leadin: One part of this event saw the raising of republican flags over the General Post Office.
swap.text: Name this failed rebellion by Sinn Fein lead by Patrick Pearse and James Connolly to establish an independent Ireland that took place during the eponymous week.
swap.clue: This poem in which William Butler Yeats memorializes "MacDonagh and MacBride / and Connolly and Pearse," who were killed as a result of an uprising.

question.text: Not affiliated with Sinn Fein was this member of the Irish Republican Brotherhood and leader of the Easter Rising, who briefly held the symbolic title of President of Ireland as he declared the creation of the Irish Republic from the steps of a post office.
question.clue: This man praised war for warming the "heart of the earth" with the "red wine of battlefields," a metaphor reflecting his mystical belief in "blood sacrifice."

swap.leadin: This battle began with a feigned retreat as the vikings of Sigurd of Orkney pretended to leave in their longboats, but instead slipped around the Munster army and disembarked in the morning.
swap.text: Identify this 1014 battle fought outside of Dublin.
swap.clue: Ulf the Quarrelsome, a prolific skull cup creator and user, allegedly killed Brodir of Man by wrapping his entrails around a tree at this battle. At this battle, the Irish under Brian Boru soundly defeated a Viking force.

question.leadin: This politician conspired with Lord Russell's Whigs to try and unseat Robert Peel in exchange for some reforms via the Lichfield House Compact.
question.text: Name this man. Parliament refused to seat him after his election to the MPship in County Clare, Ireland, until this man's agitations got the Catholic Emancipation Act passed.
question.clue: Among this man's political projects were the signing of the Lichfield House Compact to form an unlikely political alliance and the organization of "monster meetings" such as the one at Tara on behalf of the Repeal Association.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the death of T.H. Burke FTPE.
swap.text: On May 6, 1882 surgical knives were used to off Burke and his boss Lord Frederick Cavendish at this site that now gives the grisly event its name.
swap.clue: Parnell was initially accused of involvement in the May 1882 murders of Lord Cavendish and his undersecretary in this Dublin location. The murders had been carried out by the nationalist terrorist group The Invincibles.
